title: Chicken Rendang
subtitle: Indonesian slow-cooked chicken in coconut and spice paste
excerpt: Chicken thighs cooked slowly in a spiced coconut milk sauce with kaffir lime leaves until the liquid reduces and the paste coats every piece. Rendang is not a curry. The sauce is meant to be thick and dry around the meat.
sourceNotes: Rendang originates from the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra and is one of the most celebrated dishes in Indonesian and Malaysian cooking. It is traditionally cooked for celebrations and can take several hours.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after cooking. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Even better the next day as the flavours deepen.

content.text: Stir constantly in the final stages. Once the coconut milk has almost fully reduced, the paste will catch and burn quickly if left alone.
Blend the onion, garlic and ginger into a smooth paste using a blender or pestle and mortar.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the paste and fry for 4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the red curry paste, turmeric and chilli flakes. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken pieces. Turn to coat in the paste and fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk. Add the kaffir lime leaves, soy sauce and palm sugar. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Cook uncovered on a medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes.
As the coconut milk reduces, stir more frequently. Cook until the sauce is very thick and coats the chicken.
Squeeze in the lime juice. Taste and add more palm sugar or soy to balance. Serve with rice.

items.symptom: Paste is burning on the wok base.
items.cause: Heat too high in the final drying-out stage.
items.fix: Lower heat immediately and stir constantly.

items.symptom: Chicken is dry after long cooking.
items.cause: Boneless thighs can overcook if the heat was too high.
items.fix: Use lower heat and check chicken at 30 minutes.

items.cause: Palm sugar can vary in intensity.
items.fix: Add more lime juice and a pinch of salt to balance.
